wins.text: Global Banking & Markets revenues of $8.2B, up 14% YoY; FICC up 17% YoY to $3.2B; Equities up 7% YoY to $3.2B
Record combined financing revenues of $2.2B in Q2 and $4.4B for H1 2024, with FICC financing up 37% YoY to $850M (near-record)
Asset & Wealth Management revenues of $3.9B, up 27% YoY; record management and other fees plus private banking and lending revenues of $3.2B; record AUS of $2.9T
Alternatives fundraising of $36B YTD with full-year target raised to exceed $50B; notable closings including $20B for private credit and ~$10B for real estate strategies
Returned $4.4B to shareholders in Q2 including $3.5B in buybacks; 9% dividend increase to $3/share; CET1 ratio of 14.8%, 90 bps above new regulatory minimum

risks.text: ROE of 10.9% in Q2 and 12.8% for H1 remains well below the firm's 15% target, with drag from enterprise platforms and below-average IB activity still weighing on returns
Stress Capital Buffer increased unexpectedly; management believes it does not reflect strategic derisking; firm plans to moderate buybacks going forward and must maintain higher capital levels
Investment banking volumes still ~20% below 10-year averages; sponsor-led M&A activity remains depressed with uncertain timing of recovery
AWM segment ROE still around 10%, below target; 60% of alts AUM not yet fee-earning; incentive fee realization has been below internal models since Investor Day
Basel III Endgame uncertainty remains unresolved; timing potentially pushed to 2025 per Fed Chair Powell comments, creating ongoing capital planning uncertainty

guidance_items.detail: Full-year alternatives fundraising target raised to exceed $50B, up from prior implied ~$40-45B pace, driven by stronger-than-anticipated H1 and current pipeline
Buyback activity to be moderated from Q2's $3.5B level given higher-than-expected SCB requirement; will manage to prudent buffer above new regulatory minimum
Full-year effective tax rate expected at approximately 22%, unchanged
AWM pretax margin at 23% for H1, tracking toward medium-term mid-20s target; no change to target
On-balance sheet principal investment portfolio (CIE) selldown target of vast majority of $12.6B by end of 2025 reaffirmed; progress expected in Q3 and Q4 2024

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Impact of presidential election uncertainty on corporate and institutional client activity levels
Competitive landscape pressures in Banking & Markets from large bank peers and regional banks expanding capital markets capabilities
Sponsor inability to monetize assets at current carrying valuations as a potential structural concern rather than cyclical delay
